data.name: Island Dash
data.detailed_description:
look & feel
IslandDash is a 3D Open-world Minigame.
It was created by a small group of people with passion and pride.

idea
We are planning Island Dash as a "work in progress" project.
In the first version the game only is a Minigame with a approximated 10-15 min gameplay time,
but with every update we will implement new cool features that will improve the games niceness.

what to expect
On your journey you are ought to collect some coconuts
with your Cococollector3000 while avoiding evil crabs,
help Pizza-Diego by bringing him some pineapples or
even catch a parrot for an old pirate.
In the current version you can expect approximately 10 to 15 minutes Gameplay,
but we are working hard to include new features and Minigames in further versions.

story
On a lovely little Island named „Porto Parmesano“ a Tourist is sleeping at the beach.
Suddenly as the Hotdog seller shouts out „Hotdogs, fresh Hotdogs!!“ the Tourist slowly awakes.
As he arrives at the Hotdog stand he realises that he lost all his money.

Now it is your job to collect some money for him.
How many calories will he remain when he finally gets his HotDog?

data.short_description: You are controlling the Tourist through the whole Island. Your goal is to collect as much money as quickly as possible, so the Tourist can buy himself a Hotdog. If you are to slow and he runs out of calories, he will die. :( Do you think you can make it?

reviews.review:
Developed by Flo Knödl, Johannes Fischer, Michael Hütter, Christoph Müller, Simon Eberl, Thomas Kern, Lukas Schönwiese, and published by Flo Knödl, Island Dash is a charming indie adventure that delivers a lighthearted tropical escape built around exploration, quick objectives, and an intentionally brief gameplay loop. The story follows a tourist vacationing on the island of Porto Parmesano whose relaxing holiday immediately turns into a race against time after discovering that all of his money has vanished. With only a dwindling calorie supply keeping him going, players must scour the island, complete odd jobs, and earn enough cash before hunger catches up with them. It is a simple narrative, but its humorous presentation establishes a fun atmosphere that never asks players to take the adventure too seriously.

The game's strongest feature is its compact open-world island, which encourages players to wander freely instead of following a rigid path. Every corner of Porto Parmesano hides another quirky activity or colorful character in need of assistance. One moment you may be collecting coconuts with an unusual harvesting machine, while the next you're avoiding hostile crabs, delivering pineapples for a local pizza maker, or helping an eccentric pirate recover escaped parrots. These varied tasks create a pleasant rhythm that keeps exploration engaging throughout the short experience. Although none of the activities are particularly complex on their own, together they provide enough variety to make the island feel lively and entertaining.

Island Dash is designed around accessibility, making it easy for newcomers to understand its mechanics within minutes. Movement is straightforward, objectives are clearly communicated, and the calorie system adds just enough pressure to keep players moving without becoming overly stressful. Since the developers estimate that a playthrough lasts around ten to fifteen minutes, the game never overstays its welcome. Instead, it functions as a quick burst of exploration that can easily be replayed for a faster completion time or simply enjoyed as a casual distraction. Its free-to-play model also works in its favor, allowing players to experience everything without the expectation of a lengthy or content-heavy adventure.

The visual presentation complements the cheerful premise with bright environments, colorful vegetation, sunny beaches, and cartoon-inspired character designs that emphasize personality over realism. While the graphics are relatively modest, they effectively capture the laid-back island atmosphere the developers were aiming for. The soundtrack and English voice work further contribute to the playful tone, helping the world feel more animated despite its small scale. The developers are also transparent about the project being a work in progress, acknowledging that optimization and additional content remain part of their long-term plans. This honesty helps set expectations and makes it clear that Island Dash is intended to grow rather than serve as a massive finished production from the outset.

Although the game's limited length means it lacks substantial depth or long-term progression, its focus on humor, exploration, and approachable gameplay allows it to accomplish exactly what it sets out to do. It offers a relaxing and amusing adventure filled with quirky objectives that can be completed in a single sitting while leaving room for future expansion. Players searching for an extensive open-world experience or mechanically demanding gameplay may find it too lightweight, but those looking for a cheerful indie title with personality and a carefree atmosphere will likely appreciate its charm. As a free experience, Island Dash succeeds as an enjoyable showcase of creative ideas and playful design that makes good use of its modest scope.

Rating: 7/10
